author: Milwaukee City Wire
title: Milwaukee Panthers tie single-game scoring record in victory over Dominican
text:
Bart Lundy Head Coach Milwaukee Panthers Men's Basketball | Milwaukee Athletics Website
Bart Lundy Head Coach Milwaukee Panthers Men's Basketball | Milwaukee Athletics Website
The Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball team matched their single-game scoring record with a 125-70 win over Dominican (Ill.) on Tuesday night at the Klotsche Center. Eight Panthers scored in double figures, marking the first time in program history this has occurred.
Amar Augillard led all scorers with 20 points, also contributing eight rebounds and three steals. Sekou Konneh finished just shy of a double-double, tallying 17 points and nine rebounds in 19 minutes of play. Seth Hubbard added 17 points along with seven rebounds and three steals.
Danilo Jovanovich recorded 14 points on perfect shooting, going 7-for-7 from the field while adding six rebounds and three assists. Faizon Fields contributed 12 points and six rebounds, making six of his seven shots. Isaiah Dorceus also scored 12 points and distributed eight assists. Josh Dixon tied his season high with 11 points, while Simeon Murchison had career highs with 10 points and three rebounds.
"Those are pretty crazy numbers when we only made six three's," head coach Bart Lundy said postgame. "I thought we got some good contributions. It's nice to be back in the win column. This is a tired and beat-up team. It's been a really long road trip over the past couple of weeks. We have been in a bunch of states, a bunch of planes, and played a bunch of really tough opponents, so it's good to see us get back on the right side of this."
Milwaukee started strong by scoring ten of the game's first twelve points and held a commanding halftime lead at 53-24. In the second half, they set a new school record by scoring 72 points after intermission.
The team's total output matched its previous single-game record for most points scored—set against Judson University in December 2015—and broke several other records during the game. The Panthers shot over sixty percent from the field (49-of-81), breaking their previous record for most field goals made in one game with forty-nine baskets.
They dominated rebounding by outpacing Dominican by thirty boards (52-22), which ranks as one of their largest margins ever recorded. Milwaukee also held significant advantages inside, outscoring Dominican eighty-two to twenty-six in paint points and forty-eight to twelve on fast breaks.
Frank Paszkowski led Dominican with seventeen points including five made three-pointers.
The Panthers will return to action after several days off for the holiday week when they face Akron on Saturday at 6 p.m.
